title: Wake Up a Seed: Parent Guide
endLine: A dry seed is alive but resting; water wakes it.

scenes.tts: A dry bean from the kitchen jar looks like a little pebble. It doesn't grow or move. So is it alive? Two bags and a damp paper towel let your child find out.
scenes.caption: A dry bean from the kitchen jar looks like a little pebble. It doesn't grow or move. So is it alive? Two bags and a damp paper towel let your child find out.
scenes.visual: Friendly schematic kitchen counter. A large dry bean and a small pebble sit still side by side. The camera moves slowly closer. Show the question 'Is this bean alive?' in large, high-contrast text.
scenes.narration: A dry bean from the kitchen jar looks like a little pebble. It doesn't grow or move. So is it alive? Two bags and a damp paper towel let your child find out.

scenes.visual: Same bean and pebble. Title 'Wake Up a Seed' appears above them for two seconds.

scenes.tts: Setup takes about twenty minutes, then two or three minutes a day for one to two weeks. Your child practices making a guess, waiting for a slow change, and checking it. And they find out that a dry seed is resting, not dead.
scenes.caption: Setup takes about twenty minutes, then two or three minutes a day for one to two weeks. Your child practices making a guess, waiting for a slow change, and checking it. And they find out that a dry seed is resting, not dead.
scenes.visual: The bean stays in the center. Three labels appear one by one with small icons: 'Guess, then check' (pencil), 'Wait for it' (calendar with ticks), 'Look closely' (eye). A small calendar strip at the bottom shows days ticking forward slowly.
scenes.narration: Setup takes about twenty minutes, then two or three minutes a day for one to two weeks. Your child practices making a guess, waiting for a slow change, and checking it. And they find out that a dry seed is resting, not dead.

scenes.tts: You need twelve to twenty large dry beans from the grocery store, like lima, pinto, or black beans. Skip red kidney beans. Add two clear zip-top bags, two paper towels, a cup of water, a spoon, tape, and a marker.
scenes.caption: You need twelve to twenty large dry beans from the grocery store, like lima, pinto, or black beans. Skip red kidney beans. Add two clear zip-top bags, two paper towels, a cup of water, a spoon, tape, and a marker.
scenes.visual: Items slide in and settle in a row on the counter: a small heap of large beans labeled 'grocery beans', a red kidney bean with an X, two clear zip bags, two paper towels, a cup of water with a spoon, tape and a marker. A garden seed packet fades in with an X: 'Not garden seed packets'.
scenes.narration: You need twelve to twenty large dry beans from the grocery store, like lima, pinto, or black beans. Skip red kidney beans. Add two clear zip-top bags, two paper towels, a cup of water, a spoon, tape, and a marker.

scenes.tts: Check for bean, pea, peanut, or soy allergies before you start. Keep beans and bags away from children under four. Stay with your child and count the beans out. If a child is choking, call nine one one.
scenes.caption: Check for bean, pea, peanut, or soy allergies before you start. Keep beans and bags away from children under four. Stay with your child and count the beans out. If a child is choking, call nine one one.
scenes.visual: Keep the materials on the counter with the adult and child in view. Show 'Check allergies' and 'Keep away from under 4s'. Show the adult counting out the beans, then show 'Choking? Call 911' in large, high-contrast text.
scenes.narration: Check for bean, pea, peanut, or soy allergies before you start. Keep beans and bags away from children under four. Stay with your child and count the beans out. If a child is choking, call nine one one.

scenes.tts: Raw beans contain natural toxins. Never taste a bean or sprout. If a child chews or swallows beans, call Poison Control. Look through the plastic. If you see fuzz, follow the guide's mold rule. Have an adult who can safely handle the bag seal it and throw it away. Never open or sniff it.
scenes.caption: Raw beans contain natural toxins. Never taste a bean or sprout. If a child chews or swallows beans, call Poison Control. Look through the plastic. If you see fuzz, follow the guide's mold rule. Have an adult who can safely handle the bag seal it and throw it away. Never open or sniff it.
scenes.visual: Show a crossed-out mouth beside the beans, then show 'Poison Control 1-800-222-1222'. Zoom in on fuzz through the plastic and show 'Follow the guide’s mold rule'. In a small inset, an adult presses the bag shut and puts it in the trash without opening or sniffing it.
scenes.narration: Raw beans contain natural toxins. Never taste a bean or sprout. If a child chews or swallows beans, call Poison Control. Look through the plastic. If you see fuzz, follow the guide's mold rule. Have an adult who can safely handle the bag seal it and throw it away. Never open or sniff it.

scenes.tts: Start by handing your child two dry beans. Ask, 'Is this alive? How could we find out?' Write down the answer in their own words.
scenes.caption: Start by handing your child two dry beans. Ask, 'Is this alive? How could we find out?' Write down the answer in their own words.
scenes.visual: Two schematic child hands hold two dry beans. A speech bubble: 'Is this alive? How could we find out?' A small notepad at lower left gets a handwritten-style line and stays on screen.
scenes.narration: Start by handing your child two dry beans. Ask, 'Is this alive? How could we find out?' Write down the answer in their own words.

scenes.tts: Fold a towel into each bag. Wet one with a spoon until it's damp but not dripping. Leave the other towel dry. Lay four to six beans a little apart in each bag. Label the bags water and no water.
scenes.caption: Fold a towel into each bag. Wet one with a spoon until it's damp but not dripping. Leave the other towel dry. Lay four to six beans a little apart in each bag. Label the bags water and no water.
scenes.visual: Fold a paper towel into each clear bag. Spoon water onto the towel in the left bag until damp. Place five spaced beans in each bag. Label the damp bag 'water' and the dry bag 'no water'.
scenes.narration: Fold a towel into each bag. Wet one with a spoon until it's damp but not dripping. Leave the other towel dry. Lay four to six beans a little apart in each bag. Label the bags water and no water.

scenes.tts: Before you set the bags aside, ask, 'What do you think will happen in each bag?' Have your child draw their guess and save it for later.
scenes.caption: Before you set the bags aside, ask, 'What do you think will happen in each bag?' Have your child draw their guess and save it for later.
scenes.visual: Keep both bags in view. Show one speech bubble with the prediction question, then a drawing of the child’s guess. Put the drawing in a folder to keep for the comparison.
scenes.narration: Before you set the bags aside, ask, 'What do you think will happen in each bag?' Have your child draw their guess and save it for later.

scenes.tts: Leave each bag open about a finger's width for air. Tape both to a bright window away from hot afternoon sun, or lay them on a counter. Check both bags daily. Add a few drops if the damp towel starts to dry.
scenes.caption: Leave each bag open about a finger's width for air. Tape both to a bright window away from hot afternoon sun, or lay them on a counter. Check both bags daily. Add a few drops if the damp towel starts to dry.
scenes.visual: Zip each bag almost shut and show the finger-wide opening in close-up. Tape both bags side by side to the window. Show the counter as another place for both bags. Later, show a spoon adding a few drops to the damp towel only.
scenes.narration: Leave each bag open about a finger's width for air. Tape both to a bright window away from hot afternoon sun, or lay them on a counter. Check both bags daily. Add a few drops if the damp towel starts to dry.

scenes.tts: Here is a question for you. When the damp bean wakes, what do you think comes out first, the root or the shoot? And which way will it grow?
scenes.caption: Here is a question for you. When the damp bean wakes, what do you think comes out first, the root or the shoot? And which way will it grow?
scenes.visual: A large close-up of one damp, swollen bean on the towel fills the right side. On the left, a high-contrast question card: 'What comes out first? Which way?' Two small arrows, one up and one down, sit unlabeled beside the bean.
scenes.narration: Here is a question for you. When the damp bean wakes, what do you think comes out first, the root or the shoot? And which way will it grow?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card and the swollen bean. The bean swells very slightly; a soft ring turns beneath the question. No answer shown.

scenes.tts: In a warm room, most beans swell within a day. A white root usually appears in three to seven days and grows down. The curved shoot follows a few days later and turns up. The dry beans stay the same.
scenes.caption: In a warm room, most beans swell within a day. A white root usually appears in three to seven days and grows down. The curved shoot follows a few days later and turns up. The dry beans stay the same.
scenes.visual: On the same two bags, show a small 'Warm room' label and a schematic calendar. Zoom in as a bean swells. A white root pushes out beside the scar and grows down. A hooked green shoot rises a few days later. The dry beans stay unchanged.
scenes.narration: In a warm room, most beans swell within a day. A white root usually appears in three to seven days and grows down. The curved shoot follows a few days later and turns up. The dry beans stay the same.

scenes.tts: After about a week, have your child predict what water will do to the dry beans. Dampen that towel and keep checking. Most of those beans will start growing, showing they were alive all along.
scenes.caption: After about a week, have your child predict what water will do to the dry beans. Dampen that towel and keep checking. Most of those beans will start growing, showing they were alive all along.
scenes.visual: Show the child’s prediction beside the 'no water' bag. A spoon dampens that bag’s towel. Update the label to 'water added'. Advance the schematic calendar before showing roots on most of those beans.
scenes.narration: After about a week, have your child predict what water will do to the dry beans. Dampen that towel and keep checking. Most of those beans will start growing, showing they were alive all along.

scenes.tts: Compare the first drawing with the beans that sprouted. Have your child point to what matched their guess. At the end, count the beans back in. Throw the beans and towels away, then wash hands with soap and water.
scenes.caption: Compare the first drawing with the beans that sprouted. Have your child point to what matched their guess. At the end, count the beans back in. Throw the beans and towels away, then wash hands with soap and water.
scenes.visual: Slide the saved drawing beside the damp bag. Circle the part of the drawing that matches the root. Show an adult counting the beans back in, throwing away the beans and used towels, and washing hands with soap and water.
scenes.narration: Compare the first drawing with the beans that sprouted. Have your child point to what matched their guess. At the end, count the beans back in. Throw the beans and towels away, then wash hands with soap and water.

scenes.tts: That pebble-like bean was never just a stone. It was alive and resting the whole time. Water is what woke it up.
scenes.caption: That pebble-like bean was never just a stone. It was alive and resting the whole time. Water is what woke it up.
scenes.visual: Back to the opening: the pebble on the left, unchanged; on the right, the same bean now with a long white root and a green hooked shoot, glowing softly.
scenes.narration: That pebble-like bean was never just a stone. It was alive and resting the whole time. Water is what woke it up.

scenes.line: A dry seed is alive but resting; water wakes it.
scenes.visual: End card with the sprouted bean faint in the background. Centered, large, high-contrast text: 'A dry seed is alive but resting; water wakes it.'
